    /\ e \notin done
    /\ holder' = e

    /\ m.drone = holder
    /\ holder \notin active

    /\ inbox' = inbox \ {m}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, done>>

    /\ count' = count - 1

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares a single congested airspace corridor
that can safely hold at most a fixed number of drones at once. A single token
circulates around the swarm (a token ring); only the drone currently holding the
token is allowed to admit itself into the corridor, which serializes admission
decisions so the shared occupancy count is updated by one drone at a time. Drones
announce their wish to enter by posting request messages into a shared mailbox;
because the radio fabric is unordered, those messages accumulate in a set and are
matched in any order, and the token itself is released into transit and can be
re-acquired by any drone (modeling reordered hand-off). A drone holding the token
admits itself only when a matching request exists and the corridor is below
capacity. Drones already in the corridor may depart at any time, freeing a slot
and marking themselves done so they do not re-request. Once every drone has finished and parked, the swarm idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of drones in the corridor never exceeds the fixed capacity and always equals the size of the active set.

nl:
A power-grid load shedder keeps a single shared load-shed record that many
regional controllers may update. To avoid lost updates when two controllers act
at once, every write goes through a compare-and-swap register: a controller first
reads the record's current version number and stages the new shed value it wants,
then commits only if the register's version still matches the version it read.
If some other controller committed in between, the version no longer matches and
the stale attempt is discarded and retried from a fresh read. Any controller may
crash silently at any point before committing; a crashed controller drops its
staged proposal and never writes again. When every controller has either
committed or crashed, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The register version always equals the number of committed updates and the register value always equals the value of the most recent committed update, so no committed update is ever lost or overwritten out of order.

    /\ enrolled = {}
    /\ used = 0

Grant(s) ==

    /\ issued' = issued \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<revoked, queue, enrolled, used>>

Revoke(s) ==
    /\ s \in issued
    /\ s \notin revoked
    /\ s \notin enrolled
    /\ revoked' = revoked \cup {s}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, queue, enrolled, used>>

Submit(i, s) ==
    /\ Len(queue) < QMAX
    /\ s \in issued
    /\ s \notin enrolled
    /\ queue' = Append(queue, [inst |-> i, stu |-> s])
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, revoked, enrolled, used>>

Enroll ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ LET h == Head(queue) IN
        /\ h.stu \in issued
        /\ h.stu \notin revoked
        /\ h.stu \notin enrolled
        /\ used < CAP
        /\ enrolled' = enrolled \cup {h.stu}
        /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, revoked>>

DropStale ==
    /\ queue # <<>>
    /\ LET h == Head(queue) IN
        \/ h.stu \in revoked
        \/ h.stu \in enrolled
    /\ queue' = Tail(queue)
    /\ UNCHANGED <<issued, revoked, enrolled, used>>

Idle ==
    /\ queue = <<>>
    /\ \A s \in Students : s \in issued
    /\ \A s \in Students : (s \in enrolled) \/ (s \in revoked)
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E s \in Students : Grant(s)
    \/ \E s \in Students : Revoke(s)
    \/ \E i \in Instances, s \in Students : Submit(i, s)
    \/ Enroll
    \/ DropStale
    \/ Idle

    /\ revoked \subseteq Students
    /\ enrolled \subseteq Students
    /\ used \in 0..CAP
    /\ queue \in Seq([inst : Instances, stu : Students])

    /\ used <= CAP
    /\ enrolled \cap revoked = {}

NEXT Next
INVARIANT AuthOK
nl:
A university course-registration system runs two independent registrar instances
(A and B) that share one common pool of course seats. Enrollment requests flow
through a single bounded work queue with backpressure: an instance may submit a
request only while the queue has room, otherwise the submission is refused. A
request may be placed only for a student who has been granted an enrollment token
by the admissions authority. Admissions can revoke a student's token before that
student is enrolled, which makes any queued request for them stale. A worker
pulls the head request from the queue and enrolls the student only if that
student's token is still granted, not revoked, not already enrolled, and a seat
remains; otherwise, if the head request is stale (revoked) or already satisfied,
the worker drops it. When all tokens are issued, the queue is empty, and every
student is either enrolled or revoked, the system idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: Every enrolled student holds a granted token, seat usage never exceeds capacity, and no student with a revoked (stale) token is ever enrolled.

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm limits how many drones may occupy a single
observation cell at once, but that limit is tunable in flight by the ground
station. A shared occupancy register (a count plus a version number) is updated
only by compare-and-swap: a drone that wants to enter or leave first reads the
register's version, then commits its change only if the version is unchanged
since its read; if another drone committed in between, the version differs and
the attempt is aborted and retried. A drone enters only when the current
occupancy is below the live capacity, and leaves by the same read-then-swap
protocol. The ground station may raise or lower the capacity at runtime, but it
refuses to set a capacity below the number of drones currently occupying the
cell.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The register's occupancy count never exceeds the current live capacity and always equals the number of drones actually inside the cell.

EXTENDS Integers, Sequences

Hubs == {"h1", "h2"}
Keys == {"lock", "alarm"}
Vals == {"a", "b"}
NONE == "none"
WMAX == 3

VARIABLES token, rec, pend, log, writes

vars == <<token, rec, pend, log, writes>>

Init ==
    /\ token = "h1"
    /\ rec = [k \in Keys |-> [val |-> "init", ver |-> 0]]
    /\ pend = [h \in Hubs |-> [key |-> "none", val |-> "none"]]
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ writes = 0

Stage(h, k, v) ==
    /\ token = h
    /\ pend[h].key = "none"
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![h] = [key |-> k, val |-> v]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, rec, log, writes>>

Commit(h) ==
    /\ token = h
    /\ pend[h].key # "none"
    /\ writes < WMAX
    /\ LET k == pend[h].key
           v == pend[h].val IN
        /\ rec' = [rec EXCEPT ![k] = [val |-> v, ver |-> rec[k].ver + 1]]
        /\ log' = Append(log, [hub |-> h, key |-> k, val |-> v])
    /\ writes' = writes + 1
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![h] = [key |-> "none", val |-> "none"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED token

Discard(h) ==
    /\ token = h
    /\ pend[h].key # "none"
    /\ pend' = [pend EXCEPT ![h] = [key |-> "none", val |-> "none"]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<token, rec, log, writes>>

PassToken ==
    /\ token' = (IF token = "h1" THEN "h2" ELSE "h1")
    /\ UNCHANGED <<rec, pend, log, writes>>

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hubs, k \in Keys, v \in Vals : Stage(h, k, v)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : Commit(h)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : Discard(h)
    \/ PassToken

    /\ token \in Hubs
    /\ rec \in [Keys -> [val : Vals \cup {"init"}, ver : 0..WMAX]]
    /\ pend \in [Hubs -> [key : Keys \cup {"none"}, val : Vals \cup {"none"}]]
    /\ log \in Seq([hub : Hubs, key : Keys, val : Vals])
    /\ writes \in 0..WMAX

NoLostUpdate ==
    /\ Len(log) = writes
    /\ \A k \in Keys :
        LET wk == SelectSeq(log, LAMBDA e : e.key = k) IN

            THEN rec[k].ver = 0 /\ rec[k].val = "init"
            ELSE rec[k].ver = Len(wk) /\ rec[k].val = wk[Len(wk)].val

nl:
A smart-home door-lock network is run by two independent controller instances
whose hubs (h1 and h2) share one common pool of configuration records, such as
the lock policy and the alarm policy. To keep concurrent edits from clobbering
one another, the hubs pass a single token around a ring; only the hub currently
holding the token may write to the shared pool. A holding hub first stages the
new value it intends to write for one record key, then commits it, which bumps
that record's version and appends the write to a shared audit log. A holding hub
may instead discard its staged edit. The token is passed along the ring so the
other hub gets its turn. Because writes are serialized through the single token,
no update is ever lost: each record always reflects the value and count of the
writes actually committed to it.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The audit log length equals the total number of committed writes, and every configuration record's version equals how many times it was written while its value equals the most recently committed write to it.

    /\ epoch = 0
    /\ dstate = [d \in Drones |-> "idle"]
    /\ reqEp = [d \in Drones |-> 0]
    /\ served = {}

Request(d) ==
    /\ dstate[d] = "idle"
    /\ d \notin served
    /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "req"]
    /\ reqEp' = [reqEp EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, epoch, served>>

Renew(d) ==
    /\ dstate[d] = "req"
    /\ reqEp[d] # epoch
    /\ reqEp' = [reqEp EXCEPT ![d] = epoch]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, epoch, dstate, served>>

Acquire(d) ==
    /\ dstate[d] = "req"
    /\ owner = NONE
    /\ reqEp[d] = epoch
    /\ owner' = d
    /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "crit"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reqEp, served>>

    /\ owner = d
    /\ dstate[d] = "crit"
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "idle"]
    /\ served' = served \cup {d}
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, reqEp>>

    /\ dstate' = [dstate EXCEPT ![d] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<owner, epoch, reqEp, served>>

    /\ dstate[d] = "crashed"
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ UNCHANGED <<epoch, dstate, reqEp, served>>

    /\ epoch' = epoch + 1
    /\ owner' = NONE
    /\ dstate' = [d \in Drones |-> IF dstate[d] = "crit" THEN "idle" ELSE dstate[d]]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reqEp, served>>

    /\ \A d \in Drones : dstate[d] \in {"idle", "crashed"}
    /\ epoch = EMAX
    /\ \A d \in Drones : (dstate[d] = "idle") => (d \in served \/ reqEp[d] = epoch)
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

    \/ \E d \in Drones : Request(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Renew(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Acquire(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Release(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Crash(d)
    \/ \E d \in Drones : Reclaim(d)

    \/ Idle

    /\ epoch \in 0..EMAX
    /\ dstate \in [Drones -> {"idle", "req", "crit", "crashed"}]

nl:
A wildfire drone surveillance swarm shares one critical uplink relay that only a
single drone may use at a time. Access is governed by an epoch-numbered
reconfiguration scheme: a drone requests the relay tagged with the current epoch,
and may seize it only if it is free and the drone's request still carries the
current epoch. When the ground station reconfigures the swarm it bumps the epoch,
evicts whoever holds the relay, and forces outstanding requesters to renew their
request under the new epoch before they can seize it. The holder releases the
relay when done. Any drone may crash silently while requesting or while holding
the relay; a silent crash leaves the relay apparently held until the swarm
detects the crashed holder and reclaims the relay. When the epoch is exhausted
and every drone has finished or crashed, the swarm idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: At most one drone ever holds the uplink relay, because only the current owner can be in the critical section and the owner field always agrees with that drone's state.

    /\ term < TMAX

    /\ nstate[leader] = "leader"
    /\ r \notin assigned
    /\ used < CAP
    /\ assigned' = assigned \cup {r}
    /\ used' = used + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<leader, term, nstate>>

    /\ term \in 0..TMAX

    /\ used \in 0..CAP
    /\ assigned \subseteq Rooms

    /\ used = Cardinality(assigned)

A hospital operating-room scheduler is run by a small cluster of scheduler nodes,
of which exactly one acts as leader and is the only node allowed to book rooms.
Leadership is established by election: when there is no live leader a follower
raises the term and becomes a candidate, and a candidate with no competing live
leader wins and becomes leader. The hospital has a fixed number of operating
rooms, and the leader may book a room only while rooms remain below capacity; a
booked room is later freed on discharge. The leader can crash silently, after
which the cluster fails over by electing a new leader from the remaining
followers. When every node has crashed, the scheduler idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The number of booked operating rooms never exceeds the fixed capacity and always equals the number of rooms actually assigned.

Amounts == {1, 2}

RECURSIVE SumSeq(_)
SumSeq(s) == IF s = <<>> THEN 0 ELSE Head(s) + SumSeq(Tail(s))

VARIABLES reg, snap, addend, log, wstate

vars == <<reg, snap, addend, log, wstate>>

Init ==
    /\ reg = [total |-> 0, ver |-> 0]
    /\ snap = [w \in Workers |-> -1]
    /\ addend = [w \in Workers |-> 0]
    /\ log = <<>>
    /\ wstate = [w \in Workers |-> "idle"]

Read(w, a) ==
    /\ wstate[w] = "idle"
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = reg.ver]
    /\ addend' = [addend EXCEPT ![w] = a]
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "reading"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, log>>

Commit(w) ==
    /\ wstate[w] = "reading"
    /\ reg.ver = snap[w]
    /\ reg' = [total |-> reg.total + addend[w], ver |-> reg.ver + 1]
    /\ log' = Append(log, addend[w])
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "done"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<snap, addend>>

Retry(w) ==
    /\ wstate[w] = "reading"
    /\ reg.ver # snap[w]
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "idle"]
    /\ snap' = [snap EXCEPT ![w] = -1]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, addend, log>>

Crash(w) ==
    /\ wstate[w] \in {"idle", "reading"}
    /\ wstate' = [wstate EXCEPT ![w] = "crashed"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<reg, snap, addend, log>>

Idle ==
    /\ \A w \in Workers : wstate[w] \in {"done", "crashed"}
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E w \in Workers, a \in Amounts : Read(w, a)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Commit(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Retry(w)
    \/ \E w \in Workers : Crash(w)

TypeOK ==
    /\ reg \in [total : 0..8, ver : 0..2]
    /\ snap \in [Workers -> (0..2) \cup {-1}]
    /\ addend \in [Workers -> {0} \cup Amounts]
    /\ log \in Seq(Amounts)
    /\ wstate \in [Workers -> {"idle", "reading", "done", "crashed"}]

nl:
A print-shop job spooler maintains one shared record of the total number of pages
printed across all presses. Worker processes add their page counts to this total
through a compare-and-swap register that pairs the total with a version number: a
worker reads the current version and the amount it intends to add, then commits
only if the register's version is still what it read; if another worker committed
in between, the version no longer matches and the worker retries from a fresh
read. Every successful commit appends its amount to a shared audit log. A worker
may crash silently before committing; a crashed worker abandons its pending add
and never writes again. When every worker has either committed or crashed, the
spooler idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The shared total always equals the sum of all logged page-count additions and its version always equals the number of logged additions, so no committed update is ever lost.

    /\ stock > 0
    /\ moves < MMAX
    /\ stock' = stock - 1
    /\ reserved' = reserved + 1
    /\ moves' = moves + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, issued>>

    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ issued' = issued + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, stock, moves>>

    /\ reserved' = reserved - 1
    /\ stock' = stock + 1
    /\ UNCHANGED <<holder, issued, moves>>

    \/ \E n \in Nodes : Reserve(n)
    \/ Dispense
    \/ Release

nl:
A blood-bank inventory tracker accounts for a fixed number of blood units, each of
which is at any moment either in available stock, reserved for a cross-match, or
already issued to a patient. Only the node currently holding a single token that
circulates around a ring of bank stations may reserve a unit, which moves it out
of stock into the reserved pool; this serializes the reservation step. A slow
laboratory step then finalizes a reservation, moving the unit from reserved to
issued; the lab may be slow — taking arbitrarily long — but it has not failed, so
reserved units simply wait until the lab completes. A cross-match that is not
needed is released, returning its unit to stock. The token is passed around the
ring so each station gets its turn.
SAFETY PROPERTY: The blood units are conserved: available stock plus reserved units plus issued units always equals the fixed total, so no unit is ever created or destroyed as it moves between pools.

---- MODULE W4Od18m8p0t2 ----
EXTENDS Integers

Hubs == {"hA", "hB"}
Zones == {"z1", "z2"}
Doors == {"d1", "d2"}
NONE == "none"
ZoneOf == [d1 |-> "z1", d2 |-> "z2"]

VARIABLES coarse, fine, hstate, target, served

vars == <<coarse, fine, hstate, target, served>>

Init ==
    /\ coarse = [z \in Zones |-> NONE]
    /\ fine = [d \in Doors |-> NONE]
    /\ hstate = [h \in Hubs |-> "idle"]
    /\ target = [h \in Hubs |-> NONE]
    /\ served = {}

AcquireCoarse(h, d) ==
    /\ hstate[h] = "idle"
    /\ d \notin served
    /\ coarse[ZoneOf[d]] = NONE
    /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![ZoneOf[d]] = h]
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![h] = d]
    /\ hstate' = [hstate EXCEPT ![h] = "hascoarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<fine, served>>

AcquireFine(h) ==
    /\ hstate[h] = "hascoarse"
    /\ LET d == target[h] IN
        /\ fine[d] = NONE
        /\ coarse[ZoneOf[d]] = h
        /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = h]
    /\ hstate' = [hstate EXCEPT ![h] = "hasfine"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, target, served>>

ReleaseFine(h) ==
    /\ hstate[h] = "hasfine"
    /\ LET d == target[h] IN
        /\ fine' = [fine EXCEPT ![d] = NONE]
    /\ hstate' = [hstate EXCEPT ![h] = "hascoarse"]
    /\ UNCHANGED <<coarse, target, served>>

ReleaseCoarse(h) ==
    /\ hstate[h] = "hascoarse"
    /\ LET d == target[h] IN
        /\ coarse' = [coarse EXCEPT ![ZoneOf[d]] = NONE]
        /\ served' = served \cup {d}
    /\ target' = [target EXCEPT ![h] = NONE]
    /\ hstate' = [hstate EXCEPT ![h] = "idle"]
    /\ UNCHANGED fine

Idle ==
    /\ \A d \in Doors : d \in served
    /\ \A h \in Hubs : hstate[h] = "idle"
    /\ UNCHANGED vars

Next ==
    \/ \E h \in Hubs, d \in Doors : AcquireCoarse(h, d)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : AcquireFine(h)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : ReleaseFine(h)
    \/ \E h \in Hubs : ReleaseCoarse(h)
    \/ Idle

Spec == Init /\ [][Next]_vars

TypeOK ==
    /\ coarse \in [Zones -> Hubs \cup {NONE}]
    /\ fine \in [Doors -> Hubs \cup {NONE}]
    /\ hstate \in [Hubs -> {"idle", "hascoarse", "hasfine"}]
    /\ target \in [Hubs -> Doors \cup {NONE}]
    /\ served \subseteq Doors

MutexOK ==
    \A d \in Doors : (fine[d] # NONE) => (coarse[ZoneOf[d]] = fine[d])

INIT Init
NEXT Next
INVARIANT MutexOK
nl:
A smart-home door-lock network is run by two independent hub instances that share
one common pool of doors, grouped into zones. To operate a door exclusively, a hub
must acquire locks hierarchically: first the coarse lock on the door's zone, and
only then the fine lock on the door itself. A hub takes the zone's coarse lock
only when it is free, then takes the target door's fine lock only while it still
holds that zone's coarse lock. When finished the hub releases the fine lock and
then the coarse lock, marking the door serviced. Because the coarse zone lock is
single-holder and the fine lock can only be taken by the coarse-lock holder, no
two hubs can ever operate the same door at once. When every door has been serviced
and all hubs are idle, the network idles.
SAFETY PROPERTY: A door's fine lock is never held by any hub unless that same hub also holds the coarse lock on the door's zone, which guarantees mutually exclusive access to each door.
